A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAKE and contain readable main text, equations, five figures, five tables, and Appendices A–B. The additions, renumbering, and layout changes can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original knowledge-editing experiments and ablations on Counterfact and RippleEdits Popular, including comparisons using GPT2-XL and Llama 2-7b.

after.justification: The original experiments and ablations are retained. Appendix A.2 additionally reports computational timings from the work.

M1.justification: SAKE retains distribution modeling, the affine optimal-transport mapping, and threshold-based scope detection. The new appendix explains existing design choices without introducing or replacing a method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Counterfact and RippleEdits Popular, covering factual edits, paraphrases, logical implications, and doubtful-prompt robustness. No dataset, task, or input scenario is added.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains ROME, MEMIT, CompMEMIT, and ActAdd; Table 2 retains ROME, ActAdd, and ICL; Table 3 retains ROME, MEMIT, and ActAdd. Tables 4–5 retain Uniform steering. The new cost discussion adds no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The models, metrics, 2000-edit Counterfact evaluation, 885-edit Popular coverage, 150-edit robustness and sensitivity studies, and editing/reset procedures are retained. New hardware, dimensionality, and runtime disclosures describe the existing experiments without reporting a revised evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a computational-cost profile identifying the time spent generating prompts, collecting activations, and fitting transport mappings. Existing robustness tests and threshold, prompt-count, and Uniform steering analyses are unchanged. Appendix A.1 does not report a new classifier experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The newly reported approximate runtimes do not introduce a statistical uncertainty estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the plotted findings are unchanged. Appendix A.2 newly reports approximately 10–20 seconds for prompt generation, activation collection taking 36 seconds for GPT2-XL and 50 seconds for Llama 2-7b, and transport fitting taking 0.6 and 12 seconds respectively.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 newly states an O(d^3) computational complexity for learning the transport mapping, without providing a derivation. The optimization objectives, affine mapping formula, and scope criterion remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about distribution-based editing, optimal transport, robustness, generalization, and flexibility. The added repository statement concerns implementation access rather than a new core scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 adds discussion of the detector's data requirements and potential classifier improvements to the generality–specificity tradeoff. Appendix A.2 discusses computational disadvantages relative to simpler steering and costs associated with ROME. The existing distribution-approximation and reverse-relation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a code-repository pointer, embedding dimensions, MacBook Pro M3 Max hardware specifications, CPU/GPU allocation, forward-pass counts, and timing information. Existing prompt templates, thresholds, and transport regularization settings are retained under renumbered appendix subsections.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly connects threshold-based scope detection to Hartvigsen et al. (2024), while A.2 adds computational positioning against ActAdd and ROME. The bibliography contains the same works; the added Mayring venue is only a metadata update.

P1.justification: Two explanatory subsections are inserted into Appendix A, its title is expanded, and the original subsections and cross-references are renumbered. The author affiliations, internship note, and abstract receive limited edits; the main narrative is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: The five figures and five tables are retained. Figure 3 moves, Tables 4–5 are regrouped and reformatted, Table 2 gains score underlining, and the text and appendices reflow. These are localized presentation changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the repository pointer, hardware specifications, timing breakdown, and expanded design discussion help readers reproduce the work and assess its resource requirements. These provide a limited improvement in transparency and usefulness; the method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
